log.msg: The finding: all sixteen layout() functions in styles/layouts/ are the SAME tree — a nest of class strings whose leaves call parts of one shared site object (web.js). Only the class-string tree differs. So a layout is not code, it is a string, and each point in the space currently costs a directory + a page.js + a nav slot. That is the token allotment Mike named.

Read of the message, by fragment: 'reached its token allotment' = constraint (do not add a 17th hand-written layout). 'infinite space between here and there' = constraint (a finite curated list is the wrong instrument). 'this fucking ui is impeding me' = direction change — the BROWSING ui is the problem, not the layouts; the catalog rail plus exhibit teaches one layout at a time and he wants to search. Deliverable is a faster loop, not more content.

Three bugs the browser found that reading could not. (1) The ruler shipped as WIDTHS alone and the 390 shot rendered 2839px tall, swamping the other four — a fill page with no height has nothing to divide and its scroll regions never engage. Screens are pairs now. (2) 'fluid' is a THIRD trap the layouts readme does not name: .flex-1 is flex 1 1 0%, so a fluid track in a wrapping row shrinks to nothing instead of wrapping — the 390 article rendered one letter wide. Every hand-written layout writes flex:1_1_24em inline for this reason; there is no utility for it. (3) The same trap then bit this page's own shell: .space-out measured 80px at a 430 viewport. Both tracks carry a real basis now.

ext/LayoutTool: 542 findings before the miniatures declared themselves, 15-20 after (zero high). C 79 / C 71 / D 68 at 1280/1920/3440 against docs at B 84-89. Ten of the remainder are framework.css's th,td padding — every page with a table gets them — three are this readme inside md.details, and dead-space is an artifact of the ignore markers. Three framework-level observations recorded in the readme, none of them this page's to fix: --measure 52em runs ~96 chars/line at 3440; heading-offset fires on every bulleted list under an h2; the table rule is ten findings on any page with a table.

assign.outcome: **A layout is now a string, and the space is browsable** — [/framework/styles/layouts/space/](/framework/styles/layouts/space/), linked from the [Layouts](/framework/styles/layouts/) rail (group: Instrument) and from its prose. Four files, 330 lines: a text format where the whole of Docs is six lines, a seed→layout generator so a point in the space is an integer rather than a directory, a ruler that renders one spec on five screens AT ONCE, and a wall of twelve seeds you can scan and click into. The spec lives in the url hash, so any point is a link. Found three traps on the way, one of them new: `fluid` — a fluid track in a wrapping row needs a real basis, and `framework.css` has no word for it.
